roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.

roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

roster.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
roster.outlook: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.

roster.name: Kenyon Sadiq
roster.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro will look to get his consistency back on track for San Francisco in Week 4 versus the Broncos. Pineiro missed a pair of extra-point tries Sunday in a win over Arizona, but he also nailed a 57-yard field goal. The veteran kicker hadn't previously struggled with PATs, making all eight over his first two games of the campaign, so his erratic boot may have just been an aberration. Denver has yielded eight field-goal attempts and seven extra-point tries through three weeks.

roster.name: Mike Washington Jr.
roster.outlook: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't seen big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, however, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.

roster.name: Malik Washington
roster.outlook: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.outlook: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua (hip) could return to action when the Rams face Philadelphia in Week 4. Nacua has missed Los Angeles' past two games due to a hip injury, but there is some hope that he can return against the Eagles. While Nacua has been out, Davante Adams has thrived statistically as the Rams' top wideout. The team's receiving corps as a whole could find success against an Eagles squad that ranks 24th in the NFL through three weeks by giving up an average of 24.0 fantasy points per game to wideouts.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery, and in his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 win. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to hit for big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.outlook: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.

roster.name: Isiah Pacheco
roster.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.

roster.name: Zachariah Branch
roster.outlook: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.

roster.name: Tyler Loop
roster.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens return home to square off against the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was perfect again in Baltimore's dramatic 34-31 victory in Brazil in Week 3, making both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four of his extra points. Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.

roster.name: Malachi Fields
roster.outlook: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

roster.name: Kyler Murray
roster.outlook: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.

roster.name: Davante Adams
roster.outlook: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.

roster.name: Kaelon Black
roster.outlook: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.

roster.name: Adonai Mitchell
roster.outlook: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.

roster.name: Dalton Schultz
roster.outlook: Dalton Schultz is coming off a disappointing 30-yard outing in Week 3 against the Colts, but he'll remain a fantasy TE1 in Week 4 against the Cowboys if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game. Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 85 receiving yards per game since Collins got hurt. The Cowboys have struggled to defend TEs, allowing three TDs while forcing only two incompletions on 19 passes to the position. If Collins returns, Schultz will maintain fantasy starter-level upside but with a lower floor due to dropping a spot in the pass-catching hierarchy.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option at best. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The veteran quarterback has yet to throw multiple touchdowns in a game this season, while his 59.1% completion rate would be a career-worst mark. Herbert is also dealing with his usual protection issues and has been sacked eight times in three contests, a pace that would see him get brought down more than 40 times for a third straight year. His top target, Ladd McConkey, should be healthier as he puts a rib injury further behind him, but as yet none of his other pass catchers have made any kind of impact. Herbert's rough year could get worse in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.outlook: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.

roster.name: Cairo Santos
roster.outlook: Cairo Santos will aim to stay solid as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Santos nailed both of his field-goal attempts and went three-for-three on PATs in Week 3 against the Eagles. The veteran kicker has now made all but one of his field-goal tries and all 10 XPAs in the first three games of the season. He'll face a Jets squad that's allowed a top-ten 6.3 fantasy points per game to kickers.

roster.name: MarShawn Lloyd
roster.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to turn things around as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Lloyd continued his disappointing season against the Falcons in Week 3, rushing four times for 11 yards and catching two of three passes for seven yards. While the inexperienced running back was hindered by a pass-heavy game script, he's still averaged just three yards per carry across 23 attempts and seen his offensive snap share decrease in each of his first three games. He'll also face a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs this year, making him a very risky play.

roster.name: Tyjae Spears
roster.outlook: Tyjae Spears was limited to three touches for the Titans in Week 3 while playing through an ankle injury. Even if he heals up ahead of a Week 4 trip to Baltimore, Spears is unlikely to crack double-digits in touches while filling his customary change-of-pace role behind Tony Pollard. The Ravens have been middling against the run but have limited RBs to just 12 receiving yards per game, so Spears is unlikely to earn much Week 4 fantasy lineup consideration outside of super-deep formats.

roster.name: Evan McPherson
roster.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He stayed perfect on the year after drilling both field-goal attempts and all three PATs during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. McPherson is now 8-for-8 on FGAs and extra-point tries, including five kicks from at least 50 yards out. He'll aim to stay hot against one of the league's best defenses, as Jacksonville allows just 12.0 points per game, which ranks first. Still, McPherson should continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities for a Bengals squad averaging 26.7 PPG (12th).

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

roster.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.

roster.name: Jake Ferguson
roster.outlook: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.

roster.name: Oronde Gadsden
roster.outlook: Oronde Gadsden didn't get a significant increase in his pass-catching assignments in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, despite injuries to Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers to have his tight ends block, which is not Gadsden's forte. While he saw a season-high 36 offensive snaps in Week 3, he only got three targets from Justin Herbert and failed to catch any of them. There still isn't any real competition for Gadsden on the roster at tight end, but fullback Alec Ingold ended up being the player who benefited most from the absences of Njoku and Kolar. Gadsden will try to prove to his new OC that he has more to offer in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Daniel Carlson
roster.outlook: Daniel Carlson could see few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Carlson has been relatively accurate in his first three games with New Orleans, converting on seven of eight extra-point attempts and four of five field-goal tries. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high-powered offense, which is currently averaging 27.0 points per game. However, Carlson is in for a tough Week 4 matchup, as the Falcons' defense has allowed just 6.7 kicking points per game this season.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.outlook: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.outlook: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.

roster.name: Malik Willis
roster.outlook: Malik Willis will be under heavy pressure when the Dolphins face the Vikings in Week 4. Willis has just one touchdown pass through three weeks and has surprisingly topped 40 yards with his legs just once. Minnesota is the heaviest blitzing team in the league, so Willis will likely need his mobility often in Week 4. Without De'Von Achane (knee) and no emerging receivers, scrambling appears his only path to production against a defense that's allowing 7.0 yards per attempt while also allowing three touchdowns with four interceptions.

roster.name: Rashod Bateman
roster.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Baltimore's 34-31 win in Week 3, finishing second on the team in yardage. However, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) returning from a one-game absence, Bateman saw his involvement dip heavily after posting a 7-88-1 line in Week 2's loss. Flowers paced the Ravens in receptions, targets, and yardage, and as long as he remains healthy, managers can expect Bateman to see similar results against Tennessee's 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs.

roster.name: Emanuel Wilson
roster.outlook: Emanuel Wilson may be moving into a timeshare at running back for Seattle heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. An early fumble by rookie Jadarian Price was partly responsible for Wilson leading the Seahawks with nine carries in a Week 3 win over Washington, with Price logging just five totes and George Holani three. With that said, Wilson managed a paltry 14 yards on his carries, so he didn't exactly make a loud statement in a bid for more work. The Chargers just gave up 154 rushing yards to Buffalo's James Cook in Week 3, so they could be vulnerable on the ground.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Terry McLaurin
roster.outlook: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

roster.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
roster.outlook: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.

roster.name: George Holani
roster.outlook: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker missed a field goal for a second straight game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. A resurgent offense under a healthy Patrick Mahomes has given the veteran kicker a solid floor in terms of PATs, and he's a perfect 10-for-10 to begin the year with at least three in each contest. Butker's two FG misses have also been from 50-plus yards, and he's a perfect 8-for-8 from shorter distances. He may not be able to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Raiders team that's allowed 18.0 points a game, seventh in the league.

roster.name: Emmett Johnson
roster.outlook: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

roster.name: Kaleb Johnson
roster.outlook: Kaleb Johnson will seek to earn more touches as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Johnson struggled to stay involved with Green Bay playing from behind in Week 3, logging just four carries for six yards and catching one of three passes for 10 yards. The former Steeler still saw his offensive snap share increase from 27 percent in Week 2 to 36 percent in Week 3, while Lloyd's share fell in the same stretch. This could open up more opportunities in the coming weeks, but not enough to start Johnson against a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs on the year.

roster.name: De'Von Achane
roster.outlook: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty continues to see a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers with it, Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.outlook: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

roster.name: Jerry Jeudy
roster.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns play host to their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He did not record a target in Cleveland's 21-18 Week 3 victory after failing to catch his only target in Week 2's win. Jeudy now owns a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through three games, and it's clear he's fallen down the offensive pecking order behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion and TE Harold Fannin Jr. He should remain on waiver wires against Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.

roster.name: Travis Hunter
roster.outlook: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense in either of Jacksonville's last two games heading into a Week 4 trip to Cincinnati. The 2025 second overall pick has been playing almost exclusively on defense, so Hunter's off the fantasy radar in formats that don't count individual defensive statistics. He's trending up as a cornerback after intercepting Drake Maye in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.

roster.name: Kayshon Boutte
roster.outlook: Kayshon Boutte has 79 yards on nine targets through three games with the Texans heading into a Week 4 home game against the vulnerable Dallas secondary. Boutte's 8.8 yards per target (YPT) trails only Jaylin Noel's 11.2 YPT among Houston's wideouts, while Xavier Hutchinson (21 targets; 5.7 YPT) and Jared Wayne (12 targets; 5.4 YPT) haven't done much with their chances. The Texans traded for Boutte in late August, so it's possible he's being brought along slowly and could start to see his role increase, especially if Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game in Week 4. Until Boutte starts getting more opportunities, the former Patriots WR will be difficult to trust in any format.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to bounce back from a quieter game as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. St. Brown finished Week 3 against the Jets with a touchdown, but other than that, he has just four catches for 19 yards. The eight targets he finished with did still tie  Jahmyr Gibbs for a team lead, so the volume remains for the pair of stars to both produce highly. St. Brown will face a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks is the 1B option in Houston's backfield, which is enough to earn flex consideration in deeper formats for Week 4 against the Cowboys. The Cowboys are giving up 114 rushing yards per game to RBs and have surrendered four TDs to the position. Marks has 29 touches this season to David Montgomery's 44. Neither RB has found much running room behind Houston's weak offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.0 yards per carry, while Montgomery is at 2.8 yards per carry. Marks scored his first touchdown of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, while Montgomery has three TDs.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Godwin had a quiet Week 3 performance (3-25-0), though he had an 85-yard touchdown reception called back for holding. The veteran wideout has struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's offense, and those struggles could be amplified with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined for the Week 4 contest. However, Godwin is in for a favorable matchup against a Packers defense that's allowed 6.7 yards per pass attempt this season.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.

roster.name: Chris Brooks
roster.outlook: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield against the Buccaneers in Week 4. Brooks failed to register a carry and caught his sole target for four yards in a Week 3 loss to Atlanta, but he did log his third straight game with a 40-plus percent snap share on offense. The fourth-year running back's consistent usage on late downs as a pass catcher and a blocker makes him a valuable asset to the Packers, but not to fantasy managers at this point in the year. Tampa Bay has allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) but the sixth-highest receiving yards (165) to RBs on the year.

roster.name: Hunter Henry
roster.outlook: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will look to return as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jefferson exited Week 3 against the Buccaneers with an ankle injury, but there don't appear to be any concerns beyond a sprain at this point. The star wideout has totaled 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season even in just five halves, and he's been a major piece of Minnesota's 3-0 start. If he is healthy, Jefferson will face a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers this campaign.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta should remain a complementary option as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4.
