LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.

roster.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
roster.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

roster.name: Caleb Douglas
roster.outlook: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.

roster.name: Trey Smack
roster.outlook: Trey Smack will have a favorable matchup as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smack went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he also had his sole field-goal attempt blocked. The rookie kicker will seek to get back on track versus a Bucs squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (12.3) to kickers this year.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.outlook: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.outlook: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.

roster.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Robinson is expected to continue operating as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 win over the Packers, rushing 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has managed to be extremely efficient when given opportunities, averaging 4.6 yards per touch. He's also in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's given up 4.8 yards per carry this season.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers enters Seattle's Week 4 clash against the Chargers having not missed a kick so far this season. Myers handled only relatively short kicks over his first two games, but he showed off his leg with a 57-yard field goal against Washington in Week 3. The veteran kicker is now 4-for-4 on FG tries and 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts this season. Opponents have gone 6-for-7 on field-goal attempts against the Chargers so far this year.

roster.name: Cam Ward
roster.outlook: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.

roster.name: Keon Coleman
roster.outlook: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Patriots. Dealing with a Week 3 ankle injury, Coleman caught a 37-yard pass on two targets, a significant decrease in volume with DJ Moore healthy. Moore dominates targets and Buffalo is a run-first offense. Facing a defense that's allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target, there may not be enough opportunities for Coleman to contribute.

free_agents.name: Bo Nix
free_agents.outlook: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Harrison Mevis
free_agents.outlook: Harrison Mevis is coming off a career-best four FGs ahead of the Rams' matchup versus Philadelphia in Week 4. After going 0-for-1 in field-goal tries over the first two weeks of the campaign, Mevis was asked to attempt four FGs versus Denver in Week 3 and made every try, including a 48-yarder. With that said, the Rams' explosive offense doesn't frequently end drives with field-goal attempts, so Mevis may struggle to see such volume moving forward. Opponents have been successful on five of six field-goal attempts versus the Eagles so far this season.

free_agents.name: Kenny Gainwell
free_agents.outlook: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.

free_agents.name: Jakobi Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston could be in danger of losing his spot as the Chargers' No. 2 wide receiver. The 2023 first-round pick leads the team with 17 targets through three games, but that volume has resulted in just a 6-64-0 line, and Johnston has been unable to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's limitations due to a rib injury. Second-year WR Tre' Harris did in Week 3, suggesting he could be about to move past Johnston in the pecking order. Johnston will have a hard time building any momentum in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Jordan Love
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Packers take on the Falcons. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he hasn't seen the field since. The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold seems to be past the glute injury that cost him some early-season action heading into Seattle's Week 4 tilt against the Chargers. Darnold returned from a one-week absence to throw for 379 yards and four touchdowns (albeit with two interceptions) in a Week 3 win against Washington. The veteran QB continued to look often to star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who logged a massive 10-128-2 receiving line on 14 targets. The Chargers have given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, 11th-most in the league.

free_agents.name: Tyler Allgeier
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.

free_agents.name: Chris Boswell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.

free_agents.name: Will Reichard
free_agents.outlook: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.

free_agents.name: Chase McLaughlin
free_agents.outlook: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones led the Colts to their first win since Week 10 of the 2025 season in Week 3 against the Texans, but he has just three touchdown passes and five turnovers heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Jones, who underwent surgery to repair a torn Achilles in December, hasn't been much of a factor with his legs, rushing for just 19 yards and has yet to score a rushing TD after notching five last season. Washington has allowed a league-high 11 passing TDs, so while Jones will be tough to trust as a starter in one-QB formats with the Colts missing last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel; IR), he's a viable option in superflex or multi-QB leagues.

free_agents.name: Pat Freiermuth
free_agents.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.

free_agents.name: Michael Mayer
free_agents.outlook: Michael Mayer saw his stint as the Raiders' starting TE come to an end in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved as a pass catcher in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean that Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.

free_agents.name: Tyler Bass
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond will look to continue his tear as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Raymond remained a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 3 against the Eagles, pulling in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Lion transfer has now garnered five or more targets in each game this season, and eclipsed 80 yards in two of three. He'll face a Jets secondary that's been tougher on WRs this season, allowing a top-five 337 receiving yards to the position so far.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench for now. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, however, and those mistakes could catch up to him against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite the fact that Brock Bowers missed the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.

free_agents.name: Antonio Williams
free_agents.outlook: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor has yet to earn much of a role as a pass catcher through his first three weeks as a Raider. While the fifth-year wide receiver does the kind of grunt work as a blocker that keeps him on the field, he's seen only 11 targets from Kirk Cousins and caught just five of them for 52 yards and zero touchdowns. With Brock Bowers making his season debut in Week 3 and immediately reclaiming his spot as the team's top target, Nailor's path to meaningful volume got even narrower. He faces a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.

free_agents.name: Spencer Shrader
free_agents.outlook: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.

free_agents.name: Ray Davis
free_agents.outlook: Ray Davis hasn't recorded a carry in consecutive weeks or a reception all season as the Bills get set to face the Patriots in Week 4. Davis logged a total of 16 offensive snaps all season, with Ty Johnson's return as a passing-down back further hindering Davis's hope for work. He remains solely an insurance policy for James Cook against a defense allowing 4.2 yards per carry.

free_agents.name: Najee Harris
free_agents.outlook: Najee Harris turned back the clock in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Harris rushed nine times for 52 yards, and may have seized the backup running back job away from both Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely heavily on the running game in Week 4 versus Arizona, though Cam Skattebo remains atop the depth chart. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.

free_agents.name: Aaron Rodgers
free_agents.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.

free_agents.name: Mack Hollins
free_agents.outlook: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz missed his first kick of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, hitting the left upright on a 43-yard field goal attempt but connecting on both his extra points. Game flow cost him opportunities, as Denver headed into halftime down 16-0 and attempted two-point conversions multiple times as part of their comeback. Lutz has converted three FGs and five extra points through three games, and his volume may not improve substantially until his offense develops some consistency. He'll take on a 49ers team in Week 4 that's allowed just 16.7 points a game, tied for third in the league.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner will look to build upon a big Week 3 performance when Seattle hosts the Chargers in Week 4. Against the Commanders this past Sunday, Barner registered season-high marks with five catches, nine targets and 69 yards. That production was particularly notable after the third-year tight end compiled just three catches on three targets for 21 yards over the first two weeks of the campaign. Barner could find additional success against the Chargers, who rank in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to tight ends so far this season.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will look to expand on his first catch of the year as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jennings brought in one of two targets for one yard against the Buccaneers in Week 3, which is promising given that he was out due to personal reasons the previous week. The veteran should continue to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver moving forward, but Justin Jefferson's injury does have a bearing on Jennings' usage. Miami has allowed a top-five 24.2 fantasy points per game to WRs this year.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram failed to catch a pass in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, as he remains stuck in a peripheral role in the passing game. The veteran TE has notched just eight targets through three games, catching five for 60 yards and a touchdown. His workload is unlikely to significantly increase if Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are dominating looks from Bo Nix. Engram will face a 49ers defense in Week 4 that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end this season.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Chig Okonkwo
free_agents.outlook: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm is third on the Titans through three weeks with eight catches and 11 targets, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has mustered a meager 55 receiving yards. His fantasy appeal is minimal for Week 4 against the Ravens, even though Baltimore's defense has allowed a TD to a TE in two of three games this season. Helm has reached 40 receiving yards in just two of 19 NFL appearances.

free_agents.name: Jameis Winston
free_agents.outlook: Jameis Winston led the Giants to an ugly victory last game against the Titans. Winston was underwhelming to say the least, though, as he passed for under 120 yards for the second-straight outing. On a positive note, he did not throw an interception, and the Giants won the contest. However, the G-Men just traded for JJ McCarthy from the Vikings, which could put some pressure on Winston to perform. Nevertheless, Winston should remain the starter for now, and the Giants have another very winnable game in Week 4 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Folk has struggled through three weeks this season, converting on just five of eight field-goal tries while making all four point-after attempts. He had his best game of the year in the Week 3 win over the Packers, making all five of his kicks (two field goals and three extra points). With Michael Penix back at the helm, Folk could see more scoring opportunities going forward. Additionally, Folk is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 7.7 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Germie Bernard
free_agents.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Marcus Mariota
free_agents.outlook: Marcus Mariota led an improbable Washington victory over the defending Super Bowl champions last game. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4, though he is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow.  Whoever lines up under center will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pat Bryant
free_agents.outlook: Pat Bryant scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, connecting with Bo Nix for a five-yard strike in the third quarter. It was one of just two catches on the night for the second-year wide receiver. Through three games, he's produced a 6-86-1 line on nine targets while adding a 16-yard gain on one carry. Bryant is well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order, but he seems to have secured the No. 3 role ahead of Troy Franklin. Bryant will look to build some momentum in Week 4 against a 49ers secondary that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Joshua Palmer
free_agents.outlook: Joshua Palmer remains a low-volume option in the Bills' run-first offense ahead of Week 4's matchup with the Patriots. Palmer failed to record a target in Week 3 and has only two on the season. He's been a deep-ball specialist on those rare looks, but facing a New England secondary that is allowing just 6.6 yards per target, Palmer isn't likely to break off a big play in Week 4.

free_agents.name: Chris Bell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Bell will hope to build on his best game of his rookie season in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. Bell posted seven targets in Week 3 after just three in the first two weeks, playing 72% of offensive snaps with Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined. Bell is the Dolphins' highest-ceiling option, but the passing game hasn't thrived under Malik Willis. Likely playing from behind, Bell could excel against a secondary that has misleading stats thanks to a Week 2 monsoon in Chicago that shut down the passing game, but Bell needs to turn potential into production before earning fantasy trust.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain a crucial part of Tampa Bay's offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Otton had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, catching three of six targets for 56 yards. Through three weeks, Otton is the only Buccaneers tight end to record a reception, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton could struggle in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to miss time, but the matchup remains favorable, as Green Bay has allowed 11.5 PPR points per game to tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.

free_agents.name: Kendrick Bourne
free_agents.outlook: Kendrick Bourne is coming off two quiet weeks heading into Arizona's Week 4 tilt versus the Giants. After posting an 8-75-0 receiving line in the season opener against the Chargers, the veteran wideout has managed a modest four catches on six targets for 33 yards combined over his subsequent two games. Bourne appears to be well behind WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride, and at least marginally behind WR Marvin Harrison, in the passing-game pecking order at the moment. There could be an opportunity to make some noise against a Giants defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to wideouts so far this season.

free_agents.name: Odell Beckham Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Odell Beckham and Braxton Berrios have been vying for the No. 4 wideout role on the Giants, though neither has a catch to date on the young season. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for both players. Winston should remain under center in Week 3 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales is one of many Patriots hindered by the team's struggling offense heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. New England has scored just 39 points in three weeks, marginally suppressed by two missed field goals, though Borregales' opportunities have been sparse. Buffalo has allowed nine extra points and six field goal attempts through three weeks, so Borregales could be busier in Week 4. Even so, there are safer options until the Patriots offense gets in gear.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.

free_agents.name: Dominic Zvada
free_agents.outlook: Dominic Zvada provided all of the offense last game for the New York Giants. Zvada connected on all four of his field goal attempts in the 12-7 triumph over the Titans. Zvada has yet to miss a field goal through three games, and could see additional opportunities in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals are allowing 27 points per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Greg Dulcich
free_agents.outlook: Greg Dulcich will look to build on Week 3's momentum in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. After just five targets in his first two weeks, Dulcich recorded seven in Week 3, logging five receptions for 55 yards. Miami's receiving room is thin, and Malik Willis will be under constant pressure from Brian Flores' heavy-blitz scheme, allowing Dulcich to work underneath. Minnesota hasn't allowed a tight end to score, but three opposing tight ends have recorded at least 50 yards, giving Dulcich moderate Week 4 potential.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.

free_agents.name: Darnell Mooney
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Mooney has two catches in each of his first three games with the Giants. Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 50 yards in any single contest. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Mooney as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.

free_agents.name: Isaiah Williams
free_agents.outlook: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets' offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 tilt against the Bears. Despite the absence of Adonai Mitchell in Week 3, Williams logged only two targets in a game where the Jets threw 37 times. While the Bears are allowing 8.5 yards per target to receivers, Williams doesn't seem likely to garner enough looks to exploit a potentially favorable matchup.

free_agents.name: Ollie Gordon II
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.

free_agents.name: Xavier Legette
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Legette (knee) is expected to operate as one of Carolina's top deep threats if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Legette was sidelined for the Week 3 loss to the Browns but showcased some big-play ability the week prior, catching a 55-yard bomb from Bryce Young. Even if Legette suits up for the Week 4 contest, he'll likely play a depth role behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (quadriceps), if active. Legette could really take advantage of a struggling Lions secondary that's allowed 10.4 yards per completion this season.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin continues to flash his versatility for the Cowboys. In addition to his standard role as the primary returner for Dallas, Turpin also rushed for a nine-yard touchdown and even caught a nine-yard pass. Despite this, Turpin remains a boom-or-bust candidate in an offense with so much firepower ahead of him on the depth chart. In Week 4, the Cowboys face a Texans defense allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt through the air, which is 25th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ty Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Ty Johnson looks to remain a passing-down option in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. In Week 3's season debut, Johnson caught all four targets for 50 yards against the Chargers-heavy volume for playing just 15 snaps. In 28 snaps last season against New England, Johnson failed to record a reception. The Patriots have allowed eight catches to opposing running backs, rendering Johnson an unappealing, low-ceiling, low-floor option.

free_agents.name: AJ Dillon
free_agents.outlook: AJ Dillon is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. While backing up Chuba Hubbard in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, Dillon accumulated 14 yards on five total touches. He will likely struggle gaining fantasy relevance without finding the end zone, as Hubbard has a firm grasp on the Panthers' backfield. However, Dillon is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Detroit defense allowing 4.5 yards per carry to opposing RBs through three weeks.

free_agents.name: Tyquan Thornton
free_agents.outlook: Tyquan Thornton is settling in as a deep option for Patrick Mahomes. After getting blanked in Kansas City's opener, Thornton has caught six passes over the last two games on seven targets, and two of those receptions have gone for 20 yards or more. He's collected 108 yards in total, and while he's still looking for his first touchdown of 2026, it would take just one defensive breakdown to free him up for a long score. Thornton's low volume will make him a risky option in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

free_agents.name: Demond Claiborne
free_agents.outlook: Demond Claiborne will remain a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Claiborne saw his first carries of the year in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, totaling three for just one yard. The rookie looks to be in a role opposite of DeeJay Dallas as Minnesota's secondary RB option, with veteran Aaron Jones holding full control while Jordan Mason is out. Claiborne will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs on the year.

free_agents.name: Cole Kmet
free_agents.outlook: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Kmet started off the season hot with two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown, but he's been unable to catch his sole target in each of the last two games. The veteran tight end is still a big part of Chicago's offense, but it's to be seen if this goes beyond blocking work. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurst is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Hurst has proved to be a valuable part of Tampa Bay's offense just three games into his rookie campaign, catching six of 14 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. With Jalen McMillan (knee) going down in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, Hurst's role could continue to expand as the season progresses. He will likely see fewer opportunities in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the matchup remains favorable, as the Packers' defense allowed 14.2 yards per completion in a Week 3 loss to the Falcons.

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson is uncertain to be able to play in the Rams' Week 4 clash against the Eagles due to a shoulder injury. Parkinson suffered the injury in Week 3 against Denver and finished the game with no catches on one target. Meanwhile, veteran Tyler Higbee put up a strong 8-62-1 line and could be poised for more opportunities even if Parkinson does end up playing. Philadelphia has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 3.0 fantasy points per game to the position, second-best in the league.

free_agents.name: Seth McGowan
free_agents.outlook: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to continue building on an impressive performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Fitzgerald was perfect in Carolina's Week 3 loss, converting on all four of his field-goal tries. On the season, he's made all seven field-goal attempts and eight of nine point-after tries. Fitzgerald expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 4, as Detroit's defense has allowed 31.7 points per game this season, despite giving up just 5.0 kicking points per game.

free_agents.name: Kendre Miller
free_agents.outlook: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite playing the second-most snaps amongst Atlanta wide receivers this season (137), Dotson has managed to catch just four of 11 targets for 41 yards. He's clearly behind Bijan Robinson and Drake London in the Falcons' offensive game plan and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Additionally, Dotson is in for a difficult Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's allowed just 6.5 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.

free_agents.name: Sione Vaki
free_agents.outlook: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's secondary running back option in Week 4 at Carolina. Vaki hasn't been able to carve out much of a role behind phenom Jahmyr Gibbs so far this season, but he did register a season-high six carries for 26 yards, along with another catch for 11 yards in Week 3. The third-year running back remains a depth option given the usage of Gibbs so far this season, so it won't matter much that the Panthers defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.

free_agents.name: Case Keenum
free_agents.outlook: Case Keenum is in line to get the start again as the Bears play the Jets. Keenum amazed in his first start since 2023, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, while rushing four times for six yards and another score. The veteran quarterback most definitely guaranteed another opportunity if starter Caleb Williams remains out with a hamstring injury, which is currently the likely scenario. Keenum will face a Mean Green defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.

free_agents.name: Roman Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 4. He caught three of six targets for 60 yards and his first touchdown of the season during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Wilson led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished second behind Darnell Washington in yardage. He has a favorable matchup versus Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs, but it's still difficult to trust him with so many mouths to feed in the Steelers' offense.

free_agents.name: Darius Slayton
free_agents.outlook: Darius Slayton has a chance to make his Colts debut in Week 4 against the Commanders in London. The former Giants WR was inactive in Week 3 after signing with Indianapolis in the wake of Alec Pierce's heel injury, which landed Pierce on IR. Slayton brings similar field-stretching capabilities to Pierce, as Slayton has a career average of 15.0 yards per catch and has topped 500 receiving yards in six of seven previous NFL seasons. If Slayton gets the green light, he would be a viable deep-league flier given his big-play potential against a Commanders defense that has allowed the third-most yards to WRs.

free_agents.name: Joey Slye
free_agents.outlook: Joey Slye missed his only field-goal attempt in tough conditions against the Giants in Week 3, and his opportunities figure to remain limited in Week 4 at Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing 26.0 points per game, but Tennessee's underwhelming offense rarely gets into scoring range, which is why Slye has attempted at least three field goals in only one of his last 14 games. Slye also has accuracy issues, as the last time he exceeded an 80% success rate on field-goal attempts was 2022.

free_agents.name: Raheim Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the rival Steelers for a divisional clash in Week 4. He took his lone carry for 17 yards and caught four of five targets for 34 yards during Cleveland's upset win in Week 3. Sanders was highly efficient with his five touches, finishing second on the team in receptions and third in targets. He should continue operating as the third-down back and in most passing situations, but his overall involvement is difficult to trust while Quinshon Judkins remains healthy. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points (22.1) and 25th in receiving yards allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield is coming off the biggest performance of his young career ahead of the Rams' Week 4 matchup in Philadelphia. Mumpfield established new professional high marks with four catches for 93 yards against Denver in Week 3, with one of his receptions going for a 48-yard touchdown. The second-year wideout logged a healthy eight targets in the loss, but important context is that Puka Nacua sat out due to a hip injury. Should Nacua be able to return in Week 4, it's reasonable to expect Mumpfield to see considerably less opportunities. Still, the Eagles have been vulnerable against wideouts and just allowed Chicago's WR duo of Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond to combine for 13 catches, 151 yards and two TDs on Monday Night Football.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.

free_agents.name: Isaiah Davis
free_agents.outlook: Despite not recording a touch to date, Isaiah Davis could have meaningful touches in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. Breece Hall (thigh) seems unlikely to play, elevating Braelon Allen to the lead back role with Davis as a secondary option. Allen hasn't shouldered a heavy load his entire career, having double-digit carries just three times, all during his rookie 2024 season. The Bears are allowing a generous 4.9 yards per carry, so even a handful of rushes for Davis could yield positive results.

free_agents.name: Tyson Bagent
free_agents.outlook: Tyson Bagent will likely be Chicago's backup quarterback again in Week 4 against the Jets. Bagent didn't get the start in Week 3 after getting next-to-no practice reps with a concussion, and Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards and two touchdowns should keep it that way. The D2 product will now only face New York's defense if something were to happen to the veteran.
